```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

EKQDA is a small toolkit for computer-assisted qualitative data analysis. A
project lives in a single SQLite file that holds your documents, your codes,
the segments of text you have coded, and your memos. You can work with a
project from R code, through the interactive Shiny app, or both.

```{r load}
library(EKQDA)
```

## Create a project and import documents

`qual_init()` creates a project database (or opens an existing one). The
examples here use temporary files; in a real project, give `qual_init()` a path
such as `"my_research.sqlite"`.

```{r init}
project <- qual_init(tempfile(fileext = ".sqlite"))

interview1 <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
interview2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
writeLines("The justice system needs reform, and equality before the law matters.",
           interview1)
writeLines("People want justice, but they also want fairness in how it is applied.",
           interview2)

qual_import_text(project, interview1, name = "interview1")
qual_import_text(project, interview2, name = "interview2")
qual_get_documents(project)
```

## Create codes and code text

```{r codes}
qual_add_code(project, "justice", "Discussions of justice", "#FF3333")
qual_add_code(project, "equality", "Mentions of equality", "#33FF33")
qual_add_code(project, "fairness", "Mentions of fairness", "#3333FF")
qual_get_codes(project)
```

`qual_apply_code()` records that a stretch of a document, given by its first
and last character positions, belongs to a code. In the app you do the same
thing by selecting text; from code you give the positions yourself.

```{r apply}
qual_apply_code(project, doc_id = 1, code_id = 1, start = 5, end = 18,
                text = "justice system")
qual_apply_code(project, doc_id = 1, code_id = 2, start = 42, end = 66,
                text = "equality before the law")
qual_apply_code(project, doc_id = 2, code_id = 1, start = 13, end = 19,
                text = "justice")
qual_apply_code(project, doc_id = 2, code_id = 3, start = 41, end = 48,
                text = "fairness")
```

## Retrieve and count coded segments

```{r retrieve}
qual_get_codings(project, code_id = 1)
qual_code_frequency(project)
qual_project_summary(project)
```

## Code co-occurrence

`qual_code_cooccurrence()` returns a matrix that shows which codes appear
together. At the default document level, a cell counts the documents in which
both codes were applied. At the segment level, it counts pairs of coded
segments that overlap in the same document. The diagonal gives the number of
documents (or segments) in which a code appears.

```{r cooc}
qual_code_cooccurrence(project)
qual_code_cooccurrence(project, level = "segment")
```

Because the result is an ordinary matrix, it can go straight into other tools,
for example as the adjacency matrix of a code network.

## The Shiny app

`qual_launch_app()` opens the graphical interface for a project. Documents can
be added and read, codes created, text coded, memos written, and coded
segments retrieved and exported to CSV, text or Word, with frequency and
co-occurrence plots on the Visualizations tab.

```{r app, eval = FALSE}
qual_launch_app("my_research.sqlite")
```

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
DBI::dbDisconnect(project$connection)
```
